classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied radius and isosceles-triangle hint to transfer the two labelled base angles to the split angle at P. Recognise that the large triangle's angle sum counts each angle twice, proving their sum is a right angle.

content.prompt:
The Greeks said that the oldest geometrical theorem stated and proved was Thales’ theorem. Thales’ theorem states:

‘An angle in a semicircle is a right angle.’

Let $AOB$ be a diameter of a circle with centre $O$. Let $P$ be any other point on the circumference. Join $AP$, $BP$ and $OP$, and let $\angle PAB=\alpha$ and $\angle PBA=\beta$.

spec.description: Unshaded circle with horizontal diameter AB, centre O, P on the upper-left circumference, chords AP and BP, and a red dashed radius OP. Ordinary source-blue outlines are rendered black under house style. No solution angles or right-angle mark are supplied.
spec.mathematics: A, O and B are collinear; OA=OB=OP. P lies on the circle above and left of O. Angle PAB is alpha and angle PBA is beta.
spec.answerVisibility: All displayed geometry and labels are permanent givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use isosceles triangles to prove that $\angle APB=90^\circ$.

answer.short:
$\angle APB=90^\circ$.

Equal radii give two isosceles triangles, so $\angle APB=\alpha+\beta$; the angle sum of $\triangle APB$ gives $2\alpha+2\beta=180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$OA=OP$ and $OB=OP$ because they are radii. Hence $\triangle AOP$ and $\triangle BOP$ are isosceles, so $\angle APO=\alpha$ and $\angle BPO=\beta$ (equal base angles).

Since $OP$ splits $\angle APB$, $\angle APB=\alpha+\beta$.

The angles of $\triangle APB$ sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}
2\alpha+2\beta&=180^\circ\\
\alpha+\beta&=90^\circ.
\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\angle APB=90^\circ$.
